newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Nanjing Post plans to offer 100 mln B shares.
newsitem.headline: Nanjing Post plans to offer 100 mln B shares.

text.p: Nanjing Post and Telecommunications Equipment Co is preparing to make an offer of 100 million B shares to list on the Shenzhen bourse, a company spokesman said on Friday.

The Shenzhen Securities Management Office has tentatively approved the issue and the firm hopes to kick off the offer by the end of this year, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
The offer requires final approval from the Securities Commission of the State Council, he added.
He said a roadshow for the issue would be launched next month, including stops in Hong Kong, Singapore and Britain.
China Southern Securities has been appointed the lead domestic underwriter for the issue, with Hoare Govett (Asia) Ltd the international coordinator, the official said.

He said Nanjing Post planned to pump the proceeds from the B share offer into its core business, the manufacturing and sale of telecommunications-related products such as photo-electric transmission equipment.
Under Chinese accounting standards, Nanjing Post has forecast a net profit of 56 million yuan for 1996, compared with 26 million yuan in 1995 and 16 million yuan in 1994, the official said.
He said the firm expects its 1996 profits to rise sharply due to increasing demand for its products and as a result of some favourable overall policy changes.
Classified as a high-tech enterprise, Nanjing Post has enjoyed a tax-break for the past three years, the official said.
Nanjing Post currently has a total share capital of 110 million state shares held by the China Post and Telecommunications Industry Corp, he said.
